description: This Java source file defines the NonMonotonicSequenceException class, an exception used within the Apache Commons Math library to signal when a sequence of numerical values is not monotonically increasing or decreasing as expected. The class includes details about the sequence direction, strictness, index of the violation, and the previous value, along with constructors and accessor methods.

classes.name: NonMonotonicSequenceException
classes.description: An exception class thrown when a sequence (either increasing or decreasing) is violated, providing details about the sequence direction, strictness, and the index of the violation.

methods.name: NonMonotonicSequenceException
methods.description: Constructor assuming a default strict increasing sequence.

methods.name: NonMonotonicSequenceException
methods.description: Constructor allowing specification of sequence direction and strictness.

methods.name: getDirection
methods.description: Returns the direction (increasing or decreasing) of the sequence.

methods.name: getStrict
methods.description: Indicates whether the sequence was required to be strictly monotonic.

methods.name: getIndex
methods.description: Returns the index of the value that violated the sequence property.

methods.name: getPrevious
methods.description: Returns the previous value in the sequence.
